solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rush towards Rome? [It’s] warmer!

indicators.note: moving towards something puts one thing right up against the next, so the second chunk follows the first

blocks.note: to rush away from danger is to flee
CE is the Church of England; the question mark admits the cheek of a church heading for Rome

explanation.surface: Someone hurrying south to Rome is told the weather there will be warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: Rome here stands for the Roman Catholic Church, and the Church of England (CE) is pictured drifting in its direction, as Anglo-Catholics were accused of doing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fleece is a soft fleecy jacket or pullover, a garment worn to keep the body warm.

clue.text: His few faults one loudly broaches?

definitions.text: His few faults one loudly broaches?

indicators.note: faults as a verb means breaks or fractures, so the letters are cracked apart and rearranged
to broach a cask is to pierce it, so one piece is driven into the middle of another

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud

explanation.surface: A wife loudly airs her husband's shortcomings for all to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters FISHWE are pierced by I and F. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: the kind of woman who loudly broaches a man's faults.
explanation.definitionFit: A fishwife is proverbially a coarse, shrill woman who berates people, so publicly airing a man's failings is exactly her stereotype.

clue.text: One who’s succeeded in broadcast once before

indicators.note: a broadcast goes out over the airwaves, so we hear the word spoken rather than see it

blocks.note: an heir is one who has succeeded to a title or estate

explanation.surface: Someone who made it big, back in the early days of radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeded' suggests triumph, but here it means inherited. HEIR, with its silent H, sounds exactly like the old word ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ere is an archaic or poetic preposition meaning prior to, so it fits a phrase meaning formerly earlier.

clue.text: Officer, one refusing to fight on his own, left

blocks.note: a CO is a conscientious objector
someone on his own is alone, lone
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An officer, a lone pacifist, is abandoned by his comrades.
explanation.walkthrough: A conscientious objector (CO) refuses military service on moral grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonel is a senior army rank, commanding a regiment, so he is a commissioned military officer.

clue.text: British don’t have to fight — that need not be understood

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
to lack something is not to have it
boxing is fighting with fists

explanation.surface: Britons are spared from fighting, and nobody needs to explain why.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase describing the answer: a black box is any system judged only by its inputs and outputs.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering and computing a black box is a device whose internal workings are hidden or irrelevant to the user.

clue.text: Boy phoning, ringing no Scottish [or] Italian number

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so one piece is surrounded by another

blocks.note: a lad is a boy
someone phoning is on the mobile, the British word for a cellphone
nae is Scots for no

explanation.surface: A lad on the phone, but not to anyone Scottish, rather to an Italian number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian number' looks like a phone number, but a number is also a song. The Scots word sits inside the phrase for phoning.
explanation.definitionFit: La donna è mobile is the famous tenor aria from Verdi's opera Rigoletto, a musical piece sung in Italian.

clue.text: It’s time unit [of] key personnel stood on two legs!

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing on something means sitting above it, so the first part comes before what follows

blocks.note: C is a musical key
HR, human resources, is the personnel department
the leg side in cricket is also called the on side, so two legs are ON ON

explanation.surface: Key staff at some firm have learned to walk upright.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also the on side, so leg can give ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronon is a proposed smallest indivisible quantum of time in physics, a hypothetical unit of duration.

clue.text: Maybe oligarch[’s] rage after charge for possessing island

indicators.note: coming after something means placed behind it, so that chunk goes at the end

blocks.note: to charge for something is to bill for it
Iona is a small island in the Scottish Hebrides
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: A Russian tycoon fumes at being charged for owning his own island.
explanation.walkthrough: The bill comes first, holding on to the island, and the rage is tacked on after.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchs are typically immensely rich businessmen, so an oligarch is an example of someone worth a thousand million.

clue.text: Seen in Roman square, a once leading British female missionary

indicators.note: something seen in a place is inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: sixteen is a square number, written XVI in Roman numerals
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was Queen Elizabeth II, a woman who formerly headed Britain

explanation.surface: A former British leader, a woman, is spotted in a piazza in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman square' looks like a piazza, but it is a square number in Roman numerals: sixteen, XVI.
explanation.definitionFit: St Francis Xavier was a Jesuit saint who spread Christianity through India and Japan, the most famous Catholic evangelist of his age.

clue.text: Medical procedure welcome before finding work

blocks.note: hi is a word of greeting
pre is the prefix meaning before
a placement is finding someone a job

explanation.surface: A patient has surgery before being welcomed back to a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a link word ordering the pieces, but it supplies PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Replacing a worn hip joint with an artificial one is a common orthopaedic operation performed by surgeons.

clue.text: Signal folder [can provide] something enthralling

blocks.note: to spell is to signify or signal, as in 'this spells trouble'
a binder is a folder for papers

explanation.surface: An office folder that somehow sends out a signal of something gripping.
explanation.walkthrough: Signal as a verb here means spell, as in dark clouds spelling rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A spellbinder is a speaker, story or performance that holds its audience fascinated as if bewitched.

clue.text: Pole, say, heading off, [finds] somewhere to go

indicators.note: when the head is taken off, the first letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a Pole is an example of a Slav

explanation.surface: A Polish traveller setting off in search of a destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' might be a stick or a point on the globe; the capital letter and 'say' show it is a Polish person, an example of a Slav.
explanation.definitionFit: Lav is short for lavatory, and 'go' is the euphemism for relieving oneself, so a toilet is where one goes.

clue.text: Driver [from] west — heading that way?

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for west
to go west is to die, so someone heading west is a goner

explanation.surface: A driver out west, heading in the same direction as the pioneers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go west' is an idiom for dying, so a person heading that way is 'a goner'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner is a person who drives a horse-drawn wagon, so he is a driver of a cart.

clue.text: Officers in reserve prepared retreats after fighting

indicators.note: placed after means following behind, so the pieces are ordered one behind the other

blocks.note: someone game for anything is ready and willing
war is fighting
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Reserve army officers get ready to fall back after a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' suggests reserve troops; it is a nature reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Game wardens are officials who patrol a wildlife reserve, protecting animals and enforcing hunting laws.

clue.text: Description of sister we understand that’s universally unpopular?

indicators.note: what we understand here is what we are told out loud, so the word comes to us by ear

blocks.note: something universally unpopular is a thing none like

explanation.surface: A sister who, it is rumoured, is disliked by everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' reads as a sibling but is a nun. 'None like' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nunlike describes someone resembling a religious sister in manner: chaste, demure and quiet.

clue.text: Surprisingly, many falling in with parking issue regulation

indicators.note: a surprising outcome is an unexpected one, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the sign for a car park

explanation.surface: A crowd, unexpectedly, supports new parking rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a matter under debate, but it means offspring, and 'regulation' of offspring is birth control.
explanation.definitionFit: Family planning is controlling how many children one has and when, and issue is a formal word for children.

clue.text: Something fashionably labelled might have had this shape

blocks.note: hep is dated slang for hip, fashionable
a labelled thing has a tag on

explanation.surface: A designer label on clothing that is shaped oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a whole phrase: a trendy item would have a 'hep tag on'. Hep is old jazz-age slang, the forerunner of hip.
explanation.definitionFit: A heptagon is a plane figure with seven sides and seven angles, a geometric form.

clue.text: Versatile accessory, awfully swanky, misfires

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters are left in a mess

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flashy fashion accessory that keeps going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accessory' suggests a handbag or scarf; here it is a gadget carried in the pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss Army knife is a folding pocket tool with many blades and gadgets, so it has many uses.

clue.text: Hit [and] stab in back

blocks.note: first meaning: a show so successful every ticket goes
second meaning: a betrayal of those who trusted you

explanation.surface: An attacker strikes and knifes someone from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The violent surface hides two figurative senses: a hit as a success and a stab in the back as treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: A sellout is both an event whose tickets are all sold, a hit, and an act of betrayal for personal gain.

clue.text: What’s most important, [having] family doctor at home

blocks.note: kin are one's family
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: The key thing is to have the family doctor making a house call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family doctor' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the central bolt or chief element on which everything else depends, the essential part.

clue.text: Working practice of French secretary upset primates

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, and in a down entry that turns the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: MO, modus operandi, is a way of working
de is French for of
a PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A French secretary's routine disturbs the monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primates' could be archbishops; here it means the apes themselves collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: Apedom is the collective world of apes, and apes are primates, so the word stands for them as a group.

clue.text: Ex-prisoner [given] word of encouragement for keeping in trim

indicators.note: to keep something in is to hold it inside, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: to pare is to trim
olé is the Spanish cheer of approval

explanation.surface: A released convict is urged on to stay fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim' looks like an adjective about fitness, but it is the verb, to cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: A parolee is someone freed from jail early under supervision, so a former inmate.

clue.text: Most lean on one, matchless all round

indicators.note: to go all round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
something matchless is the best

explanation.surface: Most people lean on one person who has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like a verb, as in leaning on a friend; it is the adjective meaning thin.
explanation.definitionFit: The boniest person is the thinnest, with bones showing, so the superlative of skinny.

clue.text: Such as refund returned periodically?

indicators.note: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept
to be returned is to be sent back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A question about money that comes back to you at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well: a refund is money due to you, and a due paid back periodically.
explanation.definitionFit: A due is something owed or payable, and a refund is exactly such an owed sum.

clue.text: Drinking too much, perhaps, [and] sharing a bit?

blocks.note: whimsical meaning: lapping up too much, as a thirsty dog laps
ordinary meaning: partly covering the same ground

explanation.surface: Someone who drinks to excess and then hands round a portion.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is invented, flagged by 'perhaps': split the word as over plus lapping, as a dog drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things overlapping have part of their extent in common, so they share a portion between them.

clue.text: Doctrine generally somewhat clumsily recalled

indicators.note: somewhat means to some extent, so only part of the text is used
to recall is to call back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the middle three letters of this word

explanation.surface: A general theory, remembered rather awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generally' shows the definition is a word for any doctrine at all, not a particular one.
explanation.definitionFit: An ism is an informal word for any distinctive doctrine, theory or ideology, from the common suffix.

clue.text: Wrongly declare one’s piece of data in note

indicators.note: this preposition says the enclosed material goes inside the other, so the outer part surrounds it

blocks.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
one is I, and one's is one is, I + S
a stat is a statistic

explanation.surface: Someone gives a false account of a single statistic in a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' looks possessive but reads as 'one is', giving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To misstate is to state something incorrectly, giving an inaccurate account of the facts.

clue.text: Handle number in retreat with minimum staff?

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a handle is slang for a name
No. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: Managing a workforce that is falling back with only a skeleton crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a verb meaning manage; it is the noun, a name or nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-man operation is run by a single person, the smallest possible workforce, hence the question mark.
